findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: getShortcut() was added as an abstract interface method with no default implementation. Every custom/out-of-tree OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against the previous interface will fail to compile/link until it implements this method, even though such a grant could safely fall back to the encoder's unknown shortcut. Add a default method (e.g. returning the unknown shortcut) to preserve compatibility.

findings.title: OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor was removed
findings.body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor present in the base version was deleted while changing the main constructor. Custom grant types or other callers that copied a Context (to wrap/extend a grant request) will no longer compile and will fail at linkage if already compiled. This is an unnecessary public API break unrelated to capturing grantType; the copy constructor should be retained and also copy the new grantType field.

findings.title: Shortcut documentation says 3 letters but encoding requires exactly 2
findings.body: The javadoc describes the shortcut as 'usually like 3-letters', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider builds a fixed 6-character prefix (2 chars session type + 2 chars token type + 2 chars grant type) and getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects any prefix whose length is not 6. A factory author following the documentation and returning a 3-letter shortcut will produce token IDs that cannot be decoded. The contract must state and enforce exactly 2 characters.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are never validated for null or length
findings.body: postInit (and the lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut) puts whatever getShortcut() returns into ConcurrentHashMaps without checking for null or for the required 2-character length. A null shortcut causes a NullPointerException from ConcurrentHashMap.put during startup/lookup, and a 1- or 3-character shortcut is silently accepted and then produces token IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Validate shortcuts at registration and fail fast with a clear error.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offset
findings.body: The encoded prefix is sessionType[0,2) + tokenType[2,4) + grantType[4,6), so the grant shortcut is substring(4,6), not substring(3,5). Additionally the check returns false when the substring equals the expected shortcut instead of when it differs. As written, for a normal ID like 'onrtac:...' substring(3,5) is 'ta', never equals 'ac', so the matcher passes for any grant type as long as the suffix is a UUID, and would fail if it ever did match. The new grant-type assertions in expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/etc. therefore test nothing.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: Line 73 repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) instead of checking rawTokenId (the message even says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' on the wrong argument in spirit). A null rawTokenId is accepted and encodeTokenId then silently produces an ID ending in ':null', which decodes to the literal string 'null' rather than failing at construction. Fix the second check to requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).
